$doc: Vyomi capability registry — GKE (Kubernetes Engine). One entry per console feature; level per substrate (nano = shared core, also dev_server/unified ingress; offline = appliance). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py. GCP ids carry no AWS-shaped probe, so every supported level lists 'tests' instead.

gcp.kubernetes.cluster.settings.title: Cluster settings (labels, release channel, logging/monitoring service, master/node version)

gcp.kubernetes.cluster.connect.title: Connect to cluster (gcloud / kubectl command)
limitations: The displayed gcloud/kubectl commands are accurate (real endpoint, cluster CA certificate), but no Kubernetes API server runs behind a cluster's endpoint — kubectl commands against it fail. A control-plane-only simulation; the data plane needs the Max-tier k3s backend.

gcp.kubernetes.cluster.private-networkin.title: Restricting cluster access by DNS / IPv4 (private clusters)
limitations: Enforces that at least one control-plane access method (DNS-based or IPv4-based) stays enabled on create and update, and the cluster's endpoint/DNS hostname reflect the choice (no public IPv4 endpoint when IPv4 access is off). Vyomi does not run a reachable control plane behind either endpoint, so there is no live network boundary for the setting to actually restrict — same caveat as gcp.kubernetes.cluster.connect. Full private clusters (no node public IPs, authorized networks) are not modeled.

gcp.kubernetes.cluster.nodes.title: Nodes (kubectl get nodes)
limitations: Kubernetes Node objects live in the cluster's API server, which Vyomi does not run. Node pools (the GKE control-plane resource) are fully modeled — see the Node pools table.

gcp.kubernetes.workloads.title: Workloads (Deployments, StatefulSets, Pods, Jobs)
limitations: Needs a live Kubernetes API server behind the cluster endpoint; below the Max tier Vyomi only models the GKE control plane (clusters and node pools).

gcp.kubernetes.secrets-configmaps.title: Secrets & ConfigMaps
limitations: Kubernetes-native Secret/ConfigMap objects live in the cluster's API server, which Vyomi does not run.

gcp.kubernetes.discovery.title: Gateways, Services & Ingress
limitations: Gateway/Service/Ingress objects live in the cluster's API server, which Vyomi does not run.

gcp.kubernetes.storage.title: Kubernetes Storage (PersistentVolumes, StorageClasses, snapshots)
limitations: PersistentVolume/StorageClass objects live in the cluster's API server, which Vyomi does not run.

gcp.kubernetes.object-browser.title: Object Browser (generic Kubernetes resource browser)
limitations: Browses live objects from the cluster's API server, which Vyomi does not run.

gcp.kubernetes.backup.title: Backup for GKE
limitations: Backup plans and on-demand backups are real create/list/get/delete resources (gkebackup.googleapis.com's projects.locations.backupPlans and .backups) that snapshot a cluster's GKE control-plane configuration (node pool shapes, version) at backup time. Not modeled: scheduled/automatic backups (backupSchedule is stored but never fires), actual pod volume data capture, and restore (RestorePlan/Restore) — only on-demand backups of cluster config.

gcp.kubernetes.config.title: Config (Config Sync / Policy Controller / fleet configuration)
limitations: GKE Enterprise fleet configuration is not implemented.

gcp.kubernetes.applications.title: Applications
limitations: Groups live Kubernetes objects by application label; needs the cluster's API server, which Vyomi does not run.

gcp.kubernetes.fleet-registration.title: Fleet registration (GKE Hub / Anthos)
limitations: GKE Hub fleet membership (gkehub.googleapis.com) is not implemented.

gcp.kubernetes.observability.title: Observability & Cost optimization
limitations: Cluster/fleet metrics, logs-based observability and cost-optimization recommendations need Cloud Monitoring data this simulator does not generate for GKE.

gcp.kubernetes.logs.title: Logs
limitations: Shows the cluster's real GKE control-plane operations (projects.locations.operations: create/delete cluster, create/delete/resize node pool, upgrades) — genuine history, not placeholder rows. Cloud Logging entries (audit logs, container/workload logs) are not generated, since there is no Kubernetes API server or log-ingestion pipeline behind a simulated cluster.
